memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"Then Moses and the Israelites sang this song to the LORD: 'I will sing to the
LORD, for he is highly exalted. Both horse and driver he has hurled into the
sea.'" - Ex 15:1 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This is the first recorded song in the Bible. Not in Eden, not at creation, but
here, on the far shore of a sea, sung by people who were slaves a week ago.

That tells us something about what songs are for. Israel did not sing because
they were musical. They sang because something had happened that ordinary speech
could not carry. There are moments when a report is not enough and you need a
song.

Notice the word "Then." It comes immediately after the last verse of chapter 14,
where they saw the mighty hand of the LORD and trusted Him. Faith moved almost at
once into worship. That is the natural order. When we truly see what God has
done, praise is not something we have to work up.

Notice too who is exalted. Not Moses, though he raised the staff. Not Israel,
though they walked through. "I will sing to the LORD, for he is highly exalted."
The song has one subject.

Paul tells believers to speak to one another "with psalms, hymns, and songs from
the Spirit" (Eph 5:19). Singing is not decoration around the real business of
faith. It is one of the ways truth settles into us.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. When did you last sing to God rather than just about Him?
2. What has God done that deserves more than a passing mention?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, You are highly exalted. Put a song in my mouth today, and let it be about
You and not about me. Amen.
